name: IntuneGet
description: A web-based tool that automates deploying Windows applications from the Winget package repository directly into Microsoft Intune. Handles the entire deployment pipeline - searching, packaging apps into .intunewin format, and uploading to your Intune tenant. Features AI-powered app discovery, auto-generated detection rules, PSADT v4 support, configurable update policies, pre-upload permission checks, and multi-channel notifications via Slack, Teams, Discord, email, and webhooks. Self-hostable via Docker with embedded SQLite.
author: Ugur Koc

securityCheck.aiSummary: Two security concerns detected: (1) data exfiltration risk from categorize-apps.js due to sending internal app metadata to OpenAI; (2) secret management risk due to usage of a highly privileged Supabase service role key and OpenAI key in environment/config. audit-duplicate-icons.mjs shows no security issues (read-only auditing script with no external data transfers). Recommend data minimization, on-prem classification where possible, and strict secret management practices to mitigate exposure.

noDataExfiltration.reason: The script transmits curated app data (winget_id, name, publisher, description, tags, category) to the OpenAI API for classification. This constitutes data exfiltration of potentially sensitive internal catalog data to an external service. Consider data minimization, on-prem or controlled classification tooling, and verify that data handling complies with organizational policies and OpenAI data usage terms.

noHardcodedSecrets.reason: The script relies on credentials supplied via environment variables: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, as well as OPENAI_API_KEY. The presence of a service role key (highly privileged) in code paths or logs, especially if the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix suggests potential frontend exposure, creates a risk of secret leakage. Ensure secrets are kept in secure vaults, never exposed to client-side contexts, rotate keys, and restrict service role permissions.
